findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide a current CFPM certificate during the inspection. The inspector tried to walk them through finding the copy they said they had online but they could not remember which company they received it from. They also stated that the current people with manager certificates were themselves and one other. A hand out was given during the inspection for the local CFPM courses/tests in the area. Ensure that there is always a CFPM available at the facility at all times that foods or food contact items are being handled.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the two sani buckets in the facility were observed low on the inspector’s test strips. The facility made new buckets of sanitizer to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times while in use at the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

Acoustic type ceiling tiles are observed in the bathrooms. Ceiling coverings should be smooth and easily cleanable. The locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. 

The kit intended for clean-up of vomit/diarrheal events is missing the chemical needed for disinfection of the affected area. The PIC was consulted and quickly ran to the store in order to acquire bleach for this procedure. They also stated that a new kit will be purchased/ordered for future use. They returned with the bleach during this inspection and was walked through its use in relation to these procedure. Ensure that the procedures needed for these events have all needed supplies available at all times moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to actuate the paper towel dispenser, recontaminating their hands. Food service began directly after this event was observed. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all food handlers properly wash their hands prior to food service, and that the hand washing procedures do not allow for re-contamination of the hands prior to food handling practices.
